explanation: Gift-giving customs in Singapore vary sharply by community rather than following one uniform rule. Chinese Singaporeans avoid clocks, items in sets of four, and white or yellow flowers (funeral associations); Malay Muslims require halal gifts and avoid alcohol or pork; Indian/Hindu Singaporeans avoid leather and alcohol. Across all groups, gifts are usually given and received with both hands (or the right hand) and not opened in front of the giver.
local_tip: When in doubt, a high-quality food gift (confirmed halal if for a Malay host) or a nicely presented item in red/gold wrapping for a Chinese host is a safe default; avoid clocks, sets of four, leather, and alcohol unless you know your host well.
regional_note: Chinese Singaporeans: avoid clocks, sets of four, sharp objects, and white/yellow flowers (funeral associations), and favor red or gold wrapping. Malay Muslims: avoid alcohol and pork, ensure gifts are halal, and give with the right hand. Indian/Hindu Singaporeans: avoid leather and alcohol, and use bright wrapping.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is highly ritualized, with strict expectations on wrapping, presentation, and reciprocation.
Business gifts are often unnecessary or even viewed with suspicion as an attempt to curry favor.
Gift-giving is welcomed but must avoid alcohol and pork and should be given with the right hand, per Islamic custom.
